The central insight: in this small sample, feeling welcomed was the dominant factor cited for returning to rehearsal.","audience":"Choir conductors, community music organisers, volunteers running induction or welcome processes.","rationale":"Why it matters: If social welcome consistently matters most to returning participants, leaders may prioritize welcoming practices and induction over technical or repertoire changes. Important uncertainty: the sample is small and informal (12 of 19 present), collected at one rehearsal; it’s descriptive rather than causal and cannot establish how widespread or durable the effect is without further measurement.","evidence":"After the October rehearsal, 12 of 19 people present answered a short question about returning; 8 mentioned the welcome, 3 mentioned the songs, and 1 mentioned both. The central insight: these concrete, low‑barrier items form a repeatable template for taster sessions aimed at hesitant adults.","audience":"Volunteer promoters, community group event organisers, amateur arts marketing volunteers producing event copy or flyers.","rationale":"Why it matters: Organisers often need a compact set of proven items to include in outreach materials; Moorfield’s notice provides an explicit, example‑based template. Important uncertainty: the checklist is drawn from one group’s notice and does not include evidence that each item improves uptake or retention in this context.","evidence":"Notice elements: “no auditions and no requirement to read music”; “first twenty minutes are a shared warm‑up; newcomers may listen before joining”; “someone arriving from work may enter quietly until 19:20”; “A first taster is free; the ordinary weekly contribution applies from the second visit.” The notice purpose: help a hesitant newcomer picture the evening."},{"title":"Committee decision without recorded rationale or measurement: the risk of unexamined operational choices","description":"The choir’s monthly meeting recorded a decision to keep the later entry window through December, but the minutes contain no account of why that choice was made. Combined with the absence of pre/post confidence surveys and no comparison with a fixed‑start rehearsal, the central insight is that the group has implemented operational changes without documenting the rationale or collecting outcome data — leaving the effect of the change unknown.","audience":"Choir committees, volunteer boards, small voluntary organisations making operational changes.","rationale":"Why it matters: When small operational choices (like later entry windows) are adopted without documented reasons or simple outcome measures, organisations miss the chance to learn whether those changes actually reduce barriers or improve retention.
